project.name: simsh
project.goal: Evolve simsh into a lightweight agent runtime kernel with a trustworthy default workspace and realistic adapter-side non-core layers, using alternating implementation, review, and design-refinement loops until the repository reaches a high-confidence complete state.

features.title: Make long-run preflight resilient to transient temp-space failures
features.description: Execution row from manual-default (manual-20260324-long-run-temp-space-preflight). Why now: The current long-run loop can misclassify actionable work as blocked when temporary-file creation fails transiently, and this repo is currently operating with less than 200 MiB free on `/System/Volumes/Data`, which makes that noise recurring rather than hypothetical.
acceptance_criteria: `bash .bagakit/long-run/check_and_resume.sh` surfaces low-space or temp-file failures as a retryable preflight outcome with a deterministic hint instead of only a raw shell failure.
A rerun after a successful tiny-write sanity check keeps `next-action.json` and `feature-list.json` consistent instead of leaving the loop in a spurious no-next-action state.
`bash .bagakit/long-run/ralphloop.sh preflight --json` or equivalent runner guidance documents the exact retry path for temp-space anomalies.
risks: Keep the runner orchestration-only; do not bury project-specific repair logic inside long-run scripts.
If temp-space failures are actually durable, the new preflight must still stop the loop clearly instead of silently masking the problem.
features.why_now: The current long-run loop can misclassify actionable work as blocked when temporary-file creation fails transiently, and this repo is currently operating with less than 200 MiB free on `/System/Volumes/Data`, which makes that noise recurring rather than hypothetical.
evidence: `.bagakit/long-run/.gen/check_and_resume.sh` now wraps `validate-long-run.sh` output and prints retryable guidance with exact `bash .bagakit/long-run/ralphloop.sh preflight --json` and `bash .bagakit/long-run/check_and_resume.sh` steps when stderr contains `No space left on device` or `cannot create temp file`.
`bash .bagakit/long-run/ralphloop.sh preflight --json` exits `0` with `workspace_writable`, `tmp_writable`, and `cache_writable` all passing after the wrapper change.
`bash .bagakit/long-run/check_and_resume.sh` exits `0` on the healthy workspace after the wrapper change and preserves the same current item selection until the row is marked done.

Under a shimmed `validate-long-run.sh` that prints `cannot create temp file for here document: No space left on device`, `bash .bagakit/long-run/check_and_resume.sh` exits non-zero and prints the exact retry path instead of only the raw shell error.

`.bagakit/long-run/.gen/initializer_prompt.md` now tells initializer agents to run `bash .bagakit/long-run/ralphloop.sh preflight --json` and one rerun of `bash .bagakit/long-run/check_and_resume.sh` before marking temp-space failures blocked.

features.title: Implement projection freshness lifecycle and explicit refresh invalidation in the reference adapter
features.description: Execution row from manual-default (manual-20260331-reference-projection-freshness-refresh). Why now: The reference adapter now exposes source and freshness metadata, but freshness is still mostly a static label rather than a real lifecycle. Without explicit stale/live/snapshot transitions and refresh or invalidation seams, adapter-side realism stalls at the presentation layer and later benchmark review cannot distinguish fresh projections from merely renamed metadata.
acceptance_criteria: The reference adapter exposes an explicit control-plane seam for projection refresh or invalidation without making `/memory`, `/resources`, or `/knowledge_base/reference` writable mounts.

Projected documents and resources can move through a deterministic freshness lifecycle such as `snapshot`, `live`, `stale`, or `updated`, and the current freshness is surfaced consistently in `_index.json`, `/memory/projections.json`, and `/memory/projections.md`.
Adapter tests cover refresh and invalidation across create, observe, checkpoint, and resume without partial metadata drift or path identity changes.
`go test ./pkg/adapter/reference ./pkg/engine/runtime` exits 0.
risks: Keep freshness lifecycle adapter-local; do not introduce new core-runtime contracts just to model projection staleness.
Do not hide refresh semantics behind implicit file writes or mutable mounts; use explicit control-plane methods and deterministic projected views.
features.why_now: The reference adapter now exposes source and freshness metadata, but freshness is still mostly a static label rather than a real lifecycle. Without explicit stale/live/snapshot transitions and refresh or invalidation seams, adapter-side realism stalls at the presentation layer and later benchmark review cannot distinguish fresh projections from merely renamed metadata.
evidence: `pkg/adapter/reference/adapter.go` now defines canonical projection freshness states plus explicit `Refresh*` and `Invalidate*` control-plane methods for documents and resources.
Refresh now preserves existing source metadata by default while invalidation marks existing projections `stale` without changing path identity or mount writeability.
Managed `/memory/summary.md` now exposes projection-freshness counts, and direct helper tests assert stale/live transitions in `/memory/projections.json` and `/resources/_index.json`.
`go test ./pkg/adapter/reference ./pkg/engine/runtime ./benchmarks/simsh_native_reference` and `go test ./...` both exited 0 after the freshness lifecycle changes.

Strengthen evidence by decoding structured views, but keep the assertions deterministic and lightweight enough to run in ordinary CI loops.
features.why_now: Once freshness and refresh semantics exist, the next risk is false confidence: the benchmark and adapter tests can still pass while only string-matching a few happy-path fragments. This review slice makes evidence completeness part of the seam, not an afterthought.

features.title: Implement an explicit workflow-transition control plane over managed `/memory` views
features.description: Execution row from manual-default (manual-20260331-reference-workflow-transition-control-plane). Why now: Current workflow state is derived only from trace evidence. That is useful, but still too weak for a realistic non-core harness layer: adapters need a minimal explicit way to pin, override, or annotate workflow transitions without turning `/memory` into a writable scratch mount or leaking product workflow logic into core.
acceptance_criteria: The reference adapter exposes a minimal workflow-transition control plane that can record explicit status or reason updates while preserving the existing trace-derived defaults.
`/memory/workflows.json`, `/memory/workflows.md`, and `/memory/status.json` surface both the current workflow status and whether it came from trace evidence or explicit adapter control-plane action.
Adapter tests cover checkpoint and resume with both trace-driven and control-plane-driven workflow transitions.
`go test ./pkg/adapter/reference ./pkg/engine/runtime` exits 0.
risks: Keep the transition model generic and adapter-local; avoid baking product-specific workflow graphs into the reference adapter.
Do not let explicit status overrides erase the underlying trace evidence that justified the transition in the first place.
features.why_now: Current workflow state is derived only from trace evidence. That is useful, but still too weak for a realistic non-core harness layer: adapters need a minimal explicit way to pin, override, or annotate workflow transitions without turning `/memory` into a writable scratch mount or leaking product workflow logic into core.
evidence: `pkg/adapter/reference/adapter.go` now adds explicit `SetWorkflowStatus` and `ClearWorkflowStatus` control-plane methods plus `status_source` and `status_reason` fields on workflow views.
Managed `/memory/workflows.json`, `/memory/workflows.md`, and `/memory/status.json` now distinguish trace-derived workflow state from control-plane overrides without discarding trace evidence.
`pkg/adapter/reference/adapter_helpers_test.go` and `pkg/adapter/reference/adapter_test.go` now cover override, clear, and checkpoint/resume behavior for workflow transition provenance.
`go test ./pkg/adapter/reference ./pkg/engine/runtime` and `go test ./...` both exited 0 after the workflow control-plane changes.

features.title: Harden session-manager lifecycle and adapter failure edges
features.description: Execution row from manual-default (manual-20260324-session-manager-adapter-failure-edges). Why now: Session lifecycle is a core kernel contract, and `pkg/engine/runtime` still leaves the lowest coverage in `Execute` and `Resume` precisely where policy narrowing, adapter phases, and closed-session recovery interact.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime ./pkg/adapter/reference` passes with new tests for create, checkpoint, resume, or close adapter failures, blank or missing session ids, and runtime rebuild behavior after adapter-managed mounts change.
Tests prove adapter-phase failures do not partially rewrite session snapshot or checkpoint state, and closed or missing sessions keep returning stable typed errors.
Coverage for `pkg/engine/runtime` improves from the current 87.1% with direct exercise of the current low branches in `Execute`, `Resume`, and `invokeAdapterPhase`.
risks: The remaining uncovered `Execute` branches are mostly lock-loss or runtime-construction fault paths that need contrived injection rather than more lifecycle contract expansion.
Future adapters can still fail runtime reconstruction by returning invalid mounts; this pass preserves prior state on failure but does not add a broader mount-validation layer.
features.why_now: Session lifecycle is a core kernel contract, and `pkg/engine/runtime` still leaves the lowest coverage in `Execute` and `Resume` precisely where policy narrowing, adapter phases, and closed-session recovery interact.
evidence: `pkg/engine/runtime/session_manager_test.go` now covers blank-id and blank-command handling, create/checkpoint/close/resume adapter failures, active-session resume no-op behavior, and read-only runtime rebuilds that keep adapter-projected `/memory` mounts available after failure.
`pkg/engine/runtime/runtime_core_additional_test.go` now rejects blank adapter IDs and unsupported adapter phases directly, lifting `applySessionAdapters` and `invokeAdapterPhase` coverage to 100.0%.

`pkg/engine/runtime/session_manager.go` now stages adapter mount updates until adapter hooks and any runtime rebuild both succeed, so observe/checkpoint/close failures no longer clear stored adapter mounts on the way out.

`go test ./pkg/engine/runtime -run 'TestSessionManager|TestApplySessionAdapters|TestInvokeAdapterPhase'`, `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime ./pkg/adapter/reference`, and `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime -cover` all exit 0, and runtime coverage rises from 87.1% to 93.8%.

Coverage for `pkg/service/httpapi` improves from the current 71.1% while preserving existing success-path and session-lifecycle behavior.
risks: Keep the handler thin; prefer small parsing or metadata fixes over pushing runtime semantics into HTTP-only code.
If root-path metadata is intentionally excluded, document and test that contract explicitly instead of leaving code and comments contradictory.
features.why_now: The HTTP integration surface still sits at 71.1% coverage, and code inspection shows `decodeOptionalJSON`, `describePathMeta`, and path extraction around `include_meta` are only partially exercised even though higher-level harnesses depend on them.
evidence: `pkg/service/httpapi/handler_test.go` now covers empty and `null` session bodies, invalid execute JSON bodies, blank commands, session override rejection, direct `describePathMeta(...)` defaults, and explicit-root `include_meta` behavior.
